title: Hotel reservation API in Express
idea: The hotel API exposes search, hold, confirm and cancel as REST endpoints, with each service call running in one database transaction.

analogy.text: A hotel reception window: the clerk checks your form, the back office updates the ledger, and any problem returns as a standard slip with a code.
analogy.breaks: A clerk forgets a repeated form; the API replays it by key.

points: Router and controller parse HTTP; the service owns rules; the repository owns SQL.
`zod` rejects bad bodies before any SQL runs, including check-out before check-in.
POST /reservations needs an Idempotency-Key; a repeated key returns the first result.
Cancel locks the row, checks status, gives back nights, and refunds only if paid.

code.title: Layered Express app
code.caption: Repository, service, controllers and error mapping in one file, on a real PostgreSQL. One Deluxe room exists per night.

walk.text: Trimmed schema: per-night inventory and reservations with a unique Idempotency-Key.
A fixed demo date keeps refunds stable; `tx` wraps each service call in one transaction.
Repository: lock nights in order, then shift `reserved` by +1 or -1 within bounds.
Service `hold`: replay a known key, else take every night or throw SOLD_OUT.
Service `cancel`: 404, 409 on a bad status, else free nights and refund.
Controllers parse with `zod` and demand the key; Express 5 forwards async throws.
Error middleware maps validation, domain, duplicate-key and unknown errors to codes.

pitfalls: Do not charge the card inside the database transaction; a slow gateway holds row locks.
Return 200 with the stored result on replay, not a fresh 201 or a 409.
Lock the reservation row before checking its status, or two cancels both refund.

quiz.q: What status does the first cancel of RS-1 print?
quiz.why: RS-1 is HELD, which is cancellable. The service frees its nights, sets CANCELLED, refunds nothing since nothing was charged, and answers 200.

takeaway: Thin controllers, rules in the service, SQL in the repository, one transaction.

starters: Why does the replay return 200 instead of 201?
How would the confirm endpoint call the payment gateway safely?
Should availability search hit the primary database or a cache?
